gaps.sentence: She cheered ___ when she heard the news.
gaps.explanation: cheer up = become happier (also transitive: cheer somebody up).

gaps.sentence: I've mixed ___ the twins' names again.
gaps.explanation: mix up = confuse one thing/person with another.

gaps.sentence: We had to call ___ the order because the kitchen had closed.
The security guard waved us ___ without checking our passes.
gaps.explanation: 'Wave somebody through' = signal them to pass a checkpoint.

gaps.sentence: Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
gaps.explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

gaps.sentence: The talks fell ___ when neither side would compromise on fishing rights.
gaps.explanation: 'Fall through' = (a plan or deal) fail to be completed.

gaps.sentence: The film didn't live up ___ my expectations.
gaps.explanation: live up TO something = be as good as expected.

gaps.sentence: The ministry tried to play ___ the incident.
gaps.explanation: play down = make something seem less important (opposite: play up).
